core_obligations: Build the auxiliary combinatorial space: let Y be the set of nonempty subsets of the index set I, verify that the subsets V_J = {A in Y : J contained in A}, for finite nonempty J, form a basis of a unique topology on Y, and prove that every open of Y determines its own minimal family (proof lines 2010-2028).

Classify the open coverings of Y in that topology, showing that a family of opens covers Y exactly when each minimal index set J_t of the open reappears as the minimal index set of one of the covering opens (proof lines 2030-2046).

Transfer opens of Y to opens of X by V_J -> U_J = intersection of the U_i for i in J extended over unions, check that the transfer sends open coverings to open coverings, and define a sheaf G on Y by G(V) = F of the corresponding open of X, verifying the sheaf axioms with the restriction maps of F (proof lines 2048-2068).

Identify the Cech complex of the covering Y = union of the V_{i} with values in G with the Cech complex of the original covering U with values in F, conclude that G is flasque from the surjectivity hypothesis on F in the statement, and finish by the vanishing of Cech cohomology of a flasque sheaf (proof lines 2070-2083).
proof_roadmap: Introduce the space Y of nonempty subsets of I with the topology generated by the sets V_J, and record that opens of Y are unions of basis opens with a unique minimal family attached (proof lines 2010-2028).
Prove the covering criterion for this topology, which is what makes the transfer of coverings below legitimate (proof lines 2030-2046).
Define the transfer of opens from Y to X and build the sheaf G on Y out of F, so that the two Cech complexes become literally equal (proof lines 2048-2078).
Read off flasqueness of G from the hypothesis of the statement and apply the vanishing of higher Cech cohomology for flasque sheaves (proof lines 2079-2082).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a vanishing criterion for Cech cohomology of an arbitrary open covering of a topological space, under a surjectivity hypothesis on the restrictions of the sheaf to arbitrary unions of intersections of the covering (statement lines 2000-2006). The proof does not manipulate the given Cech complex directly. It invents an auxiliary space: Y is the set of nonempty subsets of the index set, topologised by the sets V_J of subsets containing a fixed finite J, and the author first has to prove that opens of Y have a uniquely determined family of minimal index sets and that a family of such opens covers Y exactly when those minimal index sets match (proof lines 2010-2046). Only then can opens of Y be transferred to opens of X by V_J mapping to the intersection of the U_i for i in J, which yields a sheaf G on Y whose Cech complex for the covering by the V_{i} is literally the given Cech complex of U with values in F (proof lines 2048-2078). The surjectivity hypothesis in the statement is exactly what makes G flasque, and the conclusion follows from the vanishing of Cech cohomology of a flasque sheaf (proof lines 2079-2082). The construction of Y and the verification that the transfer of opens behaves well are what a routine computation of a Cech complex would have avoided, and they are the substance of the proof.
